solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Minister, old man with tale that has no ending (6)

indicators.note: the tale loses its final letter

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father, PA

annotation.surface: A clergyman's elderly father spinning a story that never finishes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minister' is the church kind here, not a government one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from Latin for shepherd, the priest who tends a flock of parishioners.

entries.clue: Friar turning up in various plays — musical contribution to worship (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'turning up' runs the word bottom to top
the letters of 'plays' come in various orders
the reversed friar sits inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: PLAYS rearranged, to be split PSAL…Y
DOM, a title for some monks and friars, read upwards

annotation.surface: A friar popping up in assorted church plays that include music for the service.
annotation.walkthrough: Dom is the honorific given to Benedictine and some other religious; the friar's title is what gets turned, not a word for friar itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Psalmody is the singing of psalms, music offered in worship.

entries.clue: Country home south of Cheltenham? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means after

blocks.note: Cheltenham is a spa town, so it is an example of a SPA

annotation.surface: A country house somewhere south of the English town of Cheltenham.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English spa town in Gloucestershire; the question mark flags it as an example of a spa. 'Country home' looks like one phrase but splits into definition and IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Iberian nation is one instance of the broad class a country names.

entries.clue: Fold Labour group after losing leader (7)

indicators.note: the group's name drops its first letter

blocks.note: MOMENTUM without its first letter M

annotation.surface: A Labour Party faction folding once its leader has gone.
annotation.walkthrough: Momentum is a left-wing campaigning group within the UK Labour Party. 'Fold' looks like a verb for collapsing, but it is the noun: an anatomical fold.
annotation.definitionFit: The omentum is a fold of the peritoneum hanging from the stomach.

entries.clue: Put together solid shape outside domestic residence (8)

indicators.note: the shape goes around the residence

blocks.note: a cone is a solid geometric shape

annotation.surface: Assembling some solid structure outside a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective for the residence, but it belongs with 'shape': a solid in geometry is a three-dimensional figure.
annotation.definitionFit: To conflate is to combine two things into one, to put them together.

entries.clue: Place of security and love is protecting a son (5)

indicators.note: 'love is' surrounds 'a son', as a guard would

blocks.note: love = O, the zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: Somewhere safe and loving, where a son is kept protected.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'love is protecting' as a sentiment; in the wordplay, 'love is' is one unit whose letters open to let the son in.
annotation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a refuge, a place of calm and safety.

entries.clue: Film director — one has dropped in at the start (7)

indicators.note: 'dropped in' comes before the I

annotation.surface: A film director whom someone has popped in to see at the beginning.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as 'one has [dropped in] at the start': I has FELL IN in front of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian director of La Dolce Vita and 8½.

entries.clue: Sacred text I had translated, having received bursary? (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters of I HAD are turned into another order
the rearranged letters take the bursary inside

blocks.note: I HAD rearranged, to be split ADI…H

annotation.surface: A scholar translating a holy book once funded by a grant.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram and the container work together: the shuffled letters of I HAD split open to take in the bursary, a less familiar answer best confirmed from crossers.
annotation.definitionFit: The Adi Granth is the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib.

entries.clue: Fellows restricted by editor’s changes (6)

indicators.note: the fellows are hemmed in by the editor's letters

blocks.note: ED = editor, plus the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: Staff kept in line by the changes an editor makes.
annotation.walkthrough: E(MEN)DS. 'Changes' is a verb here, matching EMENDS.
annotation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to change or correct it.

entries.clue: Reveal end of world is nigh (8)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'world'

annotation.surface: An apocalyptic preacher announcing that the end of the world is nigh.
annotation.walkthrough: The doom-laden slogan hides three plain pieces; 'end of world' gives just one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean making known something that was hidden.

entries.clue: Ideas came about in schools (9)

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: Where new ideas were born: in the schools.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Came about' reads as a phrasal verb meaning happened; split it, and 'about' alone does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Academies are schools; in Britain the word names a kind of state school.

entries.clue: Learning to control current in river (5)

indicators.note: the learning holds the current inside, keeping it in check

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: Learning to manage the current when swimming in a river.
annotation.walkthrough: LO(I)RE. 'Current' sits naturally with 'river', but it is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: France's longest waterway, flowing past the châteaux to the Atlantic.

entries.clue: Artist, fellow out of this world (5)

blocks.note: ET = extraterrestrial, a being from beyond this world

annotation.surface: Praise for a painter whose work is simply out of this world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' reads as praise, but it is taken literally: an alien, ET.
annotation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter.

entries.clue: Handler of money paper boss sacked (9)

blocks.note: ED = editor, the boss of a newspaper

annotation.surface: A newspaper's cash handler being fired by the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the boss did the sacking; in fact the boss is ED and 'sacked' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To be cashiered is to be dismissed, originally from the armed forces in disgrace.

entries.clue: Corruption of company manager’s first seen in witness statement (13)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'manager’s'
CO and M appear inside the statement

blocks.note: a deposition is a witness's sworn statement

annotation.surface: Corporate corruption, starting with the manager, exposed in a witness's testimony.
annotation.walkthrough: DE(CO M)POSITION. 'Corruption' means rotting here, not fraud.
annotation.definitionFit: Corruption in the old sense is decay, which is decomposition.

entries.clue: Angry about one insect in food item (9)

indicators.note: CROSS goes around the one

annotation.surface: Someone furious about finding a bug in their food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the insect inside the food, but it only links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A croissant is a food item, a crescent-shaped pastry.

entries.clue: Angry as one affected by atmosphere in high church? (8)

definitions.text: affected by atmosphere in high church?

blocks.clueFragment: affected by atmosphere in high church?
blocks.note: high-church services burn incense, so a worshipper there is filled with its smoke

annotation.surface: A worshipper riled by the smoky air of a high church service.
annotation.walkthrough: High church is the ritual-heavy wing of Anglicanism, where incense is burnt. The second reading takes INCENSED literally: wreathed in incense.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for enraged; the second is a whimsical literal reading, treated with incense.

entries.clue: Book on trendy resort (8)

annotation.surface: Booking a stay at a fashionable holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast. 'Book' is the noun abbreviation, not the verb of reserving.
annotation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known English seaside resort.

entries.clue: Bird, cosy chatterer at sea (13)

indicators.note: at sea = confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A friendly, talkative bird out over the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a shore bird perfectly, which hides that it means muddled.
annotation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading bird of coasts.

entries.clue: Dweller on Ibiza maybe not one for unjustified defamation? (7)

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out

blocks.note: Ibiza is an island, so one living there is an islander

annotation.surface: Asking whether an Ibiza resident was wrongly defamed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that Ibiza is just one example of an island.
annotation.definitionFit: Slander is false, spoken defamation of someone.

entries.clue: Special sandals mostly elevated above air (7)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: an air is a tune, an aria

annotation.surface: Platform sandals raising the wearer up into the air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests flight, apt for winged sandals, but it is a song.
annotation.definitionFit: Talaria are the winged sandals of the god Hermes (Mercury).

entries.clue: Some members of old law society upset ancient king (6)

indicators.note: take some of the letters of the phrase
in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down

annotation.surface: Some senior lawyers upsetting an old monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: Oswald was a seventh-century king of Northumbria, later a saint.
annotation.definitionFit: Saint Oswald was an Anglo-Saxon king of Northumbria.

entries.clue: Canadian city before long hosting a card game (9)

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the first part holds the second within it

blocks.note: skat is a German card game

annotation.surface: A Canadian city soon to host a card tournament.
annotation.walkthrough: S(A SKAT)OON. Saskatoon is the largest city in Saskatchewan.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest city of Saskatchewan, on the South Saskatchewan River.

entries.clue: Female potentially shocking? Nothing on top! (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the O goes above LIVE

blocks.note: a live wire can give an electric shock

annotation.surface: A woman who might shock by wearing nothing on top.
annotation.walkthrough: The topless joke hides an electrical one: a live wire is potentially shocking. 'Female' stands for a woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woman's given name, as borne by Popeye's sweetheart Olive Oyl.

entries.clue: Deceitful, not upright (5)

annotation.surface: A dishonest, crooked character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not upright' reads as not honest, repeating the first sense; it actually means lying flat.
annotation.definitionFit: Lying means both untruthful and horizontal.

entries.clue: Report of old city’s section of canal (5)

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Ilium is the Latin name of ancient Troy

annotation.surface: A report on an old city's stretch of canal.
annotation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, the gut, not a waterway.
annotation.definitionFit: The ileum is the last section of the small intestine, part of the alimentary canal.

entries.clue: Ace child looked after trophy? (5)

blocks.note: a child placed under a guardian's care

annotation.surface: A brilliant child earning a trophy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ace' reads as an adjective praising the child, but it is the card abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a trophy is one kind of prize.

entries.clue: Home, comfortable one housing organ, seriously! (2,7)

indicators.note: the organ goes inside, between the two parts

blocks.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable home
the ear is an organ of hearing

annotation.surface: A cosy home with an organ in it, said with full sincerity.
annotation.walkthrough: IN + NEST houses EAR: IN(EAR)NEST. 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a body part.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means with sincere intent, not joking.

entries.clue: Investigator made a mistake, being put off (8)

annotation.surface: A detective's blunder getting him taken off the case.
annotation.walkthrough: DET + ERRED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discouraged from acting, usually by fear of the consequences.

entries.clue: Meat good in the morning first day back at work? (6)

blocks.note: Monday, the first day of the working week

annotation.surface: A good meat breakfast on the first morning back at work.
annotation.walkthrough: Gammon is cured ham, a British staple. The question mark flags MON as Monday by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Gammon is a cut of cured pork, a meat.
